# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## Primary Classification by Core Mechanic

---

### 1. LOOP DRAWING GAMES
*Objective: Draw a single continuous closed loop through the grid*

#### 1.1 Unconstrained Path Loop
- **Slitherlink** — Loop drawn between dots; numbers indicate surrounding line count
- **Masyu** — Loop must satisfy black circle (turn + straight) and white circle (straight + turn neighbor) rules

#### 1.2 Cell-Traversal Loop
*Loop passes through cell centers*

##### 1.2.1 With Regional Constraints
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop visits rooms once; must alternate between moon-only and sun-only rooms
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop must go straight or turn through ALL white circles in each bold-bordered area; avoids black circles
- **Suraromu** — Loop starts/ends at numbered circle; must pass through all "Gates" in specified order

##### 1.2.2 With Directional/Wind Constraints
- **Nagareru** — Loop direction constrained by wind arrows in black cells; cannot move against wind

##### 1.2.3 With Circle/Midpoint Constraints
- **Mid-loop** — Loop must pass through black circles such that each circle is the exact midpoint of a straight segment

##### 1.2.4 With Black Cell Constraints
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids black cells and numbered arrow cells; arrows indicate black cell counts in a direction

---

### 2. REGION/AREA DIVISION GAMES
*Objective: Partition the grid into defined regions or blocks*

#### 2.1 Division into Rectangles/Squares
- **Shikaku** — Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number indicating its cell count
- **Choco Banana** — Divide into regions; black cells form rectangles/squares, white cells must not

#### 2.2 Division into Polyominoes
- **Fillomino** — Divide into blocks where each block's number equals its size; same-size blocks cannot touch
- **LITS** — Color one tetromino per bold region; same-shape tetrominoes cannot touch; colored cells must connect
- **Norinori** — Place dominoes (pairs) of black cells; each bold region gets exactly two black cells
- **Nuritwin** — Each region contains two same-size blocks of shaded cells; all shaded cells connect across regions

#### 2.3 Division into L-Shaped Blocks
- **Sashigane** — Divide into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends, arrows mark ends pointing toward bend

#### 2.4 Division with Color Pairing
- **Double Choco** — Divide into blocks each containing matching white and gray sub-areas of identical shape

#### 2.5 Division into Fixed-Size Blocks
- **Five Cells** — Divide grid into pentominoes (exactly 5 cells each); numbers indicate surrounding block-edge count

---

### 3. CELL SHADING/COLORING GAMES
*Objective: Determine which cells to paint black (or color)*

#### 3.1 Constraint-Based Shading with Connectivity Rules
- **Nurikabe** — Black cells form connected wall; white cell islands sized by given numbers; no 2×2 black squares
- **Heyawake** — Shade cells per room counts; no two shaded cells adjacent; white cells cannot span more than two rooms in a line
- **Hitori** — Shade cells so no number repeats in any row/column; shaded cells cannot touch; white cells stay connected
- **Kurodoko** — Shade cells such that numbered white cells count exactly their visible white cells in four directions

#### 3.2 Shading with Sum/Count Constraints
- **Kurotto** — Circles indicate sum of contiguous black cells extending from them in four directions
- **Usowan** — Shade cells; each bold region has exactly one number that is intentionally wrong; shaded cells cannot connect

#### 3.3 Shading with Geometric Shape Constraints
- **Choco Banana** — Black groups must be rectangular; white groups must not be rectangular
- **Shakashaka** — Place triangular half-cell shading; remaining white areas must form rectangles/squares
- **Tilepaint** — Color entire "Tiles" (bold regions) black or white; diagonal-numbered cells indicate black cell counts in row/column segments

#### 3.4 Shading with Gravity/Physical Constraint
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells in rooms per room numbers; when "dropped" downward, shaded cells fill exactly the bottom half

#### 3.5 Shading with Maze Constraints
- **Nurimeizu** — Shade whole rooms to create a maze from S to G; circles must lie on shortest path; triangles must not; no 2×2 uniform squares

---

### 4. NUMBER PLACEMENT GAMES
*Objective: Fill cells with numbers satisfying defined constraints*

#### 4.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness Constraints
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box exactly once

#### 4.2 Regional Number Sets
- **Ripple Effect** — Each bold room contains 1 through N (room size); duplicate values in a row/column must be separated by at least that value's distance
- **Makaro** — Each room contains 1 through N; arrow black cells indicate which adjacent cell holds the largest value; same numbers in adjacent rooms cannot touch

#### 4.3 Block-Size Labeling
- **Fillomino** — Numbers label block sizes; filled and given numbers must be consistent *(also listed under Region Division)*
- **Chained Block** — Black cell blocks labeled by size; blocks must chain (touch at corners); chain cannot repeat same shape

#### 4.4 Crossword-Style Number Fitting
- **Nansuke** — Fill white cells with digits from a given number list; numbers run horizontally or vertically

#### 4.5 Snake/Sequential Placement
- **Hebi** — Place sequences 1–5 forming "snakes" in white cells; snakes cannot touch; vision rules restrict placement based on arrow clues in black cells

---

### 5. CONNECTION/PATH GAMES
*Objective: Connect elements or trace paths without crossing*

#### 5.1 Island Bridge Connection
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with 1–2 bridges per pair; bridges cannot cross; all islands must form one connected network

#### 5.2 Paired Cell Connection
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-branching lines that fill the grid

#### 5.3 Circle/Token Movement
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles into their home regions; numbered circles move exactly that many cells; paths cannot cross
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles into gray areas via straight arrows; gray area totals must match sum of entering circles

---

### 6. SYMBOL/MARK PLACEMENT GAMES
*Objective: Place specific symbols according to structural rules*

#### 6.1 Light/Illumination Placement
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs in white cells; numbered cells indicate adjacent bulb count; every white cell must be illuminated; bulbs cannot illuminate each other

#### 6.2 Directional Mark Filling
- **Juosan** — Fill every cell with — or |; territorial number clues indicate excess of one mark type; — cannot stack more than 2 rows; | cannot span more than 2 columns

#### 6.3 Promontory (Endpoint) Placement
- **Nurimisaki** — Circles mark promontory cells (exactly one white neighbor); numbered circles indicate length of white line from that cell; white cells connect; no 2×2 uniform blocks

---

### 7. SHAPE EVOLUTION / SEQUENTIAL BLOCK GAMES
*Objective: Place or grow shapes following sequential rules*

- **Evolomino** — Draw squares in cells forming blocks; each block contains one pre-drawn arrow; each successive block along an arrow's route adds one square to the prior block's shape
- **Pencils** — Identify pencil shapes (straight strips with a tip); draw lines from tips through a number of cells equal to the pencil's number

---

## Summary Cross-Reference Table

| Game | Primary Mechanic | Key Distinguishing Feature |
|---|---|---|
| Akari | Symbol Placement | Illumination/line-of-sight |
| Chained Block | Number Placement | Block chains, no repeated shapes in chain |
| Choco Banana | Region Division + Shading | Black=rectangle, White≠rectangle |
| Dotchi-Loop | Loop Drawing | All-or-nothing circle traversal per region |
| Double Choco | Region Division | Paired white/gray mirror shapes per block |
| Evolomino | Shape Evolution | Blocks grow by one cell along arrow routes |
| Five Cells | Region Division | Fixed pentomino size; edge-count clues |
| Fillomino | Region Division + Numbers | Block size = number label |
| Hashiwokakero | Connection | Bridge counts; single connected network |
| Hebi | Number Placement | Sequential snakes with vision attack rules |
| Heyawake | Cell Shading | Room counts; white cell span limit |
| Hitori | Cell Shading | No repeated numbers per row/column |
| Juosan | Symbol Placement | Directional marks (—/|) with territory balance |
| Kurodoko | Cell Shading | Numbered cells count their white visibility |
| Kurotto | Cell Shading | Circle = sum of adjacent black cell runs |
| LITS | Region Division | One tetromino per region; global connectivity |
| Masyu | Loop Drawing | Black/white circle turn rules |
| Nagareru | Loop Drawing | Wind direction constrains loop movement |
| Nansuke | Number Placement | Crossword-style number list fitting |
| Norinori | Region Division | Dominoes; two per region |
| Nurimeizu | Cell Shading | Whole-room shading; maze with path constraints |
| Nurimisaki | Symbol Placement | Promontory cells; white line lengths |
| Makaro | Number Placement | Room sets 1–N; arrow picks largest neighbor |
| Mid-loop | Loop Drawing | Black circles must be midpoints of straight segments |
| Moon-or-Sun | Loop Drawing | Alternating moon/sun rooms; one visit per room |
| Numberlink | Connection | Pair matching; non-crossing paths |
| Nurikabe | Cell Shading | White islands + connected black wall |
| Nuritwin | Region Division + Shading | Two equal blocks per region; global shading connectivity |
| Pencils | Shape Placement | Straight pencil bodies; line length = number |
| Ripple Effect | Number Placement | Room sets 1–N; spacing rule for duplicates |
| Sashigane | Region Division | L-shaped blocks only |
| Satogaeri | Circle Movement | One circle per region; numbered movement distance |
| Shakashaka | Symbol Placement | Half-cell triangles; white remainder = rectangles |
| Shikaku | Region Division | Rectangles only; one number per rectangle |
| Slitherlink | Loop Drawing | Dot-connected loop; cell edge count clues |
| Sto-stone | Cell Shading | Gravity drop; bottom-half fill constraint |
| Sudoku | Number Placement | Row/column/box uniqueness |
| Suraromu | Loop Drawing | Gate-crossing sequence from numbered start |
| Tilepaint | Cell Shading | Whole-tile coloring; diagonal clue cells |
| Usowan | Cell Shading | One deliberately wrong number per region |
| Yajilin | Loop Drawing | Arrow clues count black cells; loop avoids black cells |
| Yosenabe | Circle Movement | Straight-line movement into gray areas; sum totals |
